desc: The Taj Mahal is a white marble mausoleum in Agra, built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1632 and 1653 in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. The structure is renowned for its symmetrical Mughal architecture, intricate pietra dura inlay work, and the stunning central dome flanked by four minarets. The complex includes formal gardens, a mosque, and a guest house. The Taj Mahal attracts over 7 million visitors annually, making it one of the most visited tourist attractions in the world. Its color appears to change throughout the day from pinkish at dawn to milky white in the evening.
fact: The Taj Mahal was built by Emperor Shah Jahan between 1632-1653 as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal · It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World · It is built entirely of white marble with intricate pietra dura inlay work · It attracts over 7 million visitors annually and changes color through the day

desc: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. Built in 1889 as the entrance arch to the 1889 World's Fair, it stands 330 meters tall, making it the tallest structure in Paris. Designed by engineer Gustave Eiffel, the tower was initially criticized by leading French artists and intellectuals. It is the most-visited paid monument in the world, with nearly 7 million visitors annually. The tower has three visitor levels with restaurants, observation decks, and the summit offering panoramic views of Paris. It was originally intended to be dismantled after 20 years but was saved by its usefulness as a radio transmission tower.
fact: The Eiffel Tower was built in 1889 for the World's Fair, standing 330 meters tall · It is the most-visited paid monument in the world with 7 million annual visitors · Designed by Gustave Eiffel, it was initially criticized by French intellectuals · It was saved from demolition by its use as a radio transmission tower

desc: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built across the northern borders of China to protect against invasions. Construction began as early as the 7th century BC, with the most famous sections built by the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644). The wall stretches over 21,000 km, making it the longest man-made structure in the world. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. The wall features watchtowers, garrison stations, and beacon towers. Contrary to popular belief, the wall is not visible from space with the naked eye. It attracts over 10 million visitors annually, with the most popular section near Beijing at Badaling.
fact: The Great Wall of China is over 21,000 km long, the longest man-made structure in the world · Construction began in the 7th century BC, with Ming Dynasty sections being the most famous · It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New Seven Wonders · The wall is not visible from space with the naked eye despite popular belief

desc: Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel situated on a mountain ridge 2,430 meters above sea level in the Eastern Cordillera of southern Peru. Built for Inca emperor Pachacuti around 1450, it was abandoned during the Spanish Conquest and remained unknown to the outside world until American historian Hiram Bingham brought it to international attention in 1911. The site features classic Inca dry-stone construction with precisely fitted stones without mortar. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. Machu Picchu is Peru's most-visited tourist attraction, drawing over 1.5 million visitors annually. The site is divided into agricultural and urban sectors with temples, terraces, and water channels.
fact: Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel at 2,430 meters in the Peruvian Andes · It was built around 1450 for Inca emperor Pachacuti · It was rediscovered by Hiram Bingham in 1911 after being abandoned for centuries · It features classic Inca dry-stone construction without mortar and is a New Seven Wonder

desc: The Colosseum is an oval amphitheatre in the center of Rome, Italy, built between 70-80 AD under Emperor Vespasian and his successor Titus. It is the largest ancient amphitheatre ever built, with a capacity of 50,000-80,000 spectators. The Colosseum was used for gladiatorial contests, public spectacles, animal hunts, and dramas based on classical mythology. It stands 48 meters tall with four stories and an elaborate system of ramps, stairs, and tunnels. Despite damage from earthquakes and stone theft, it remains a iconic symbol of Imperial Rome and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It is one of the New Seven Wonders of the World and attracts over 7 million visitors annually.
fact: The Colosseum was built between 70-80 AD, the largest ancient amphitheatre ever built · It held 50,000-80,000 spectators for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles · It stands 48 meters tall with four stories and an elaborate underground tunnel system · It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World

desc: Christ the Redeemer is a 30-meter-tall Art Deco statue of Jesus Christ in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Built between 1922 and 1931, it stands atop the 710-meter Corcovado Mountain in the Tijuca National Park. The statue weighs 635 metric tons and is made of reinforced concrete clad in soapstone. It is the largest Art Deco sculpture in the world and one of the most recognizable symbols of Brazil. With arms stretching 28 meters wide, the statue appears to embrace the city below. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World. The statue is struck by lightning several times each year and attracts over 2 million visitors annually.
fact: Christ the Redeemer is a 30-meter Art Deco statue atop 710-meter Corcovado Mountain in Rio de Janeiro · Built 1922-1931, it weighs 635 metric tons in concrete and soapstone · It is the largest Art Deco sculpture in the world and a New Seven Wonder · Its arms stretch 28 meters wide, appearing to embrace the city of Rio de Janeiro
